LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension, part of Strand 6 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we read for comprehension? 2. Why do people take part in economic activities in the society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read texts on the theme,

2. identify vocabulary related to the theme – economic activities,

3. pick out verbs from the text and list them down,

4. create a vocabulary list of words related to the theme,

5. work with peers to find the meaning of the words,

6. work with peers to create mind maps to establish other words related to the new words (e.g. opposites, synonyms),

7. construct sentences using vocabulary and verbs related to economic activities,

8. answer direct and inferential questions from comprehension passages related to the theme. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read texts on the theme,
2. identify vocabulary related to the theme – economic activities,
3. pick out verbs from the text and list them down,
4. create a vocabulary list of words related to the theme,
5. work with peers to find the meaning of the words,
6. work with peers to create mind maps to establish other words related to the new words (e.g. opposites, synonyms),
7. construct sentences using vocabulary and verbs related to economic activities,
8. answer direct and inferential questions from comprehension passages related to the theme. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by identifying vocabulary related to

the theme.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: The learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning when creating mind maps to

establish other words related to the new words.

Values:
• Love: This is promoted as the learner respects others when working to find the meaning of the words.

• Social Justice: The is promoted as the learner fosters inclusivity of ideas when working with peers to create mind maps to

establish other words related to the new words (e.g. opposites, synonyms).

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Poverty: This is addressed as the learner interacts with texts and passages on economic activities to get creative ideas for

poverty eradication.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate their knowledge of verbs to the concept of word classes in English and Kiswahili.
